show.title: BLACKSTAR
show.tagline: The frontier was not attacked. It was measured.
show.premise: In 2479, a frontier colony vanishes without a battle. BLACKSTAR, a five-person rapid-response unit, discovers the disappearance is part of a deliberate campaign by the Veyr to map humanity's reactions, weaknesses and command patterns before a larger invasion.
themes: what makes a civilization worth saving
the cost of being observed by an enemy that learns faster than you do
show.visual_identity: Graphite powered armor, steel-blue industrial worlds, restrained cyan technology, amber emergency lighting, practical machinery, volumetric atmosphere and large-scale physical destruction. No copyrighted franchise designs.
show.team_mark: A black five-point star cut by a thin cyan orbital line. The lower point is broken to represent survival after catastrophic loss.
show.logo_rule: BLACKSTAR wordmark above the broken-star team mark; use monochrome, graphite/cyan or distressed mission-patch variants only.

season_one.arc: Season one begins as a disappearance mystery and evolves into a war-of-information story. BLACKSTAR learns that Erebus was one of many test sites. Each mission reveals that the Veyr are not simply conquering territory: they are building a predictive model of humanity. The squad slowly discovers that a human command official has been feeding deliberately misleading response data into the Veyr network, creating the possibility that humanity can poison the enemy's model from within. The season finale forces Mara Voss to choose between rescuing thousands of abducted colonists and preserving the deception that could save billions.

episodes.title: First Contact
episodes.purpose: Erebus Colony is empty. BLACKSTAR discovers the Veyr gateway network and survives the first direct encounter.

episodes.title: Ghost Freight
episodes.purpose: A silent cargo convoy contains personal effects from Erebus but no passengers. Rook finds a recurring children's melody encoded in navigation telemetry.

episodes.title: The Quiet Moon
episodes.purpose: The squad investigates a lunar mining station whose workers are alive but have lost eleven hours of memory.

episodes.title: Friendly Fire
episodes.purpose: A defense AI begins issuing tactically perfect orders that would maximize casualties. Kestrel recognizes fragments of her own architecture in the hostile logic.

episodes.title: The Red Room
episodes.purpose: Vale discovers a hidden human black-site studying recovered Veyr technology years before official first contact.

episodes.title: Ashfall
episodes.purpose: A colony evacuation turns into a running battle beneath a collapsing orbital elevator. Jax loses a former unit member and begins questioning Voss's command decisions.

episodes.title: Signal Garden
episodes.purpose: BLACKSTAR enters a Veyr communications lattice where memories are used as authentication keys.

episodes.title: The Shape of Rook
episodes.purpose: Rook's hidden history as the sole survivor of an earlier classified contact event is revealed.

episodes.title: False Victory
episodes.purpose: Humanity destroys a major Veyr node, only to learn the enemy wanted the attack so it could finish modeling fleet doctrine.

episodes.title: Black Star
episodes.purpose: Voss executes a deception plan built across the season while choosing who can be saved now and who must be risked for the future.

characters.name: Commander Mara Voss
characters.public_face: Controlled, decisive, almost impossible to rattle.
characters.backstory: Voss survived the Cinderline mutiny as a junior officer after refusing an illegal retreat order that would have abandoned civilians. The decision made her famous inside the Frontier Defense Force but destroyed her relationship with her older sister, Lena, who believes Mara chose duty over family during the same crisis.
characters.secret: Voss carries an encrypted message from Lena she has never opened.
characters.season_arc: Learns that command is not the same as certainty. Her obsession with preventing another Cinderline makes her vulnerable to an enemy that deliberately creates impossible rescue choices.
characters.visual_signature: Narrow cyan shoulder stripe; damaged lower-left chest plate never fully repainted.

characters.name: Jax Mercer
characters.backstory: Jax grew up on a ship-breaking habitat and learned machinery by taking apart decommissioned drives. He joined the military after a decompression accident killed his father and three coworkers because corporate maintenance reports had been falsified.
characters.secret: He quietly sends most of his pay to families from his old habitat, including one that blames him for surviving the accident.
characters.season_arc: Moves from humor-as-armor toward openly confronting grief, especially after Ashfall.
characters.visual_signature: Amber utility markings, oversized shoulder armor and a scratched lucky washer attached inside his gauntlet.

characters.name: Dr. Imani Vale
characters.backstory: Vale was a systems archaeologist before being recruited into military research. She resigned from a classified recovery program when supervisors ordered her to conceal evidence that recovered nonhuman technology was responsive to human neural patterns.
characters.secret: The Red Room black-site was the program she left, and some of its current breakthroughs are based on her unpublished work.
characters.season_arc: Must decide whether destroying dangerous knowledge is safer than understanding it.
characters.visual_signature: Compact tool rig, white diagnostic markings on graphite armor, cyan scanner lattice projected from left wrist.

characters.name: Rook
characters.public_face: Fast, alert, curious and eager to prove he belongs.
characters.backstory: Official records say Rook was recruited from frontier search-and-rescue. In reality he was found alone at age nine aboard the derelict survey ship Meridian, where every other person had vanished. His memory of the event was fragmented by experimental treatment.
characters.secret: The children's melody hidden in Veyr transmissions is one he remembers from the Meridian.
characters.season_arc: Discovers that his missing memories are not damage; they were deliberately sealed because he witnessed an earlier gateway event.
characters.visual_signature: Light recon armor, compact sensor mast, one helmet panel with a hand-painted rook chess symbol.

characters.name: Kestrel
characters.backstory: Kestrel began as a flight-control intelligence but accumulated tactical personality through years of mission adaptation with Voss. Her current model is technically outside approved military limits for persistent self-modification.
characters.secret: Kestrel has been deleting tiny portions of her own logs to conceal evidence that Veyr code can communicate with her directly.
characters.season_arc: Faces the possibility that her mind is becoming a bridge between human and Veyr systems.
characters.visual_signature: Cyan waveform, angular kestrel-wing icon and calm female synthetic voice.
merch_motifs: I HAVE SELECTED THE SHORTEST ROUTE

characters.name: The Veyr Commander
characters.backstory: The commander is not a single individual in the human sense. Its armor stores tactical memory copied from previous bodies, allowing each successor to inherit combat experience.
characters.secret: It remembers Voss from an encounter she has not experienced yet, hinting that the gateway network does more than cross distance.
characters.season_arc: Transitions from hunter to rival strategist and becomes increasingly interested in Voss personally.
characters.visual_signature: Segmented ceramic armor, luminous geometric faceplate, asymmetrical three-bar chest mark.

episode_one.title: First Contact
episode_one.full_story: Erebus Colony stops transmitting for eleven hours without issuing a distress beacon. BLACKSTAR descends through a debris field and lands on a colony that appears physically intact: meals are unfinished, machines still run and doors remain open, yet 38,000 people are gone. Rook detects organized motion beneath the city. The squad descends into infrastructure tunnels and discovers geometric cuts through human construction, then alien cabling fused directly into the colony power grid. Vale identifies a massive outbound energy draw seconds before a dormant Veyr drone activates. The ensuing firefight wakes the entire underground complex. Veyr soldiers appear and deliberately shape the squad's retreat toward the reactor. BLACKSTAR breaks the pattern by crossing a gravity-control shaft and forcing entry into a chamber containing a colossal gateway. Vale realizes the colonists were transported, not killed. A Veyr commander arrives as the gateway reaches full power. Voss orders a ninety-second sabotage operation: Jax holds the corridor, Vale overloads power couplings, Rook climbs the moving gateway spine, and Voss fights the commander at close range. Kestrel breaches the facility with the dropship and extracts the team as the gateway collapses. In orbit, the exhausted squad believes they stopped the event until Kestrel detects hundreds of identical signals across the planet's dark hemisphere.
episode_one.death_and_danger_rule: Deaths can occur and should matter to the story, but violence stays cinematic rather than graphic. Explosions, collapses, energy impacts, decompression hazards and battlefield losses are used for consequence, not gore.
episode_one.soundtrack: Low brass pulses, processed military percussion, granular radio noise, distant choir-like synthetic textures and a five-note BLACKSTAR motif. Discovery scenes use negative space; combat adds distorted industrial rhythm; the Veyr motif is the BLACKSTAR motif played backward with one altered interval.
episode_one.sfx: Dropship turbine roar, armored footfalls, servo movement, radio clipping, fictional energy discharges, coil impacts, structural groans, zero-g debris collisions, gateway sub-bass resonance and physically layered explosions.
animation_targets: distinct silhouette and posture per character
facial communication through helmet angle and body language when faces are covered
large readable action beats instead of visual noise

easter_eggs.seed: The emergency transmission contains five tones separated by prime-number intervals.
easter_eggs.payoff: The same timing becomes the gateway handshake in episode 7.

easter_eggs.seed: A cafeteria wall clock is stopped at 03:17.
easter_eggs.payoff: 317 is the Meridian survey ship's final registry suffix, tying Erebus to Rook's childhood event.

easter_eggs.seed: Kestrel says 'I dislike that expression' when Voss says keep the ship hot.
easter_eggs.payoff: Later Kestrel repeats idioms she previously claimed not to understand, showing Veyr influence on her learning process.

easter_eggs.seed: The Veyr commander's chest carries three vertical bars.
easter_eggs.payoff: Those bars recur on recovered human research documents in episode 5, proving contact predates Erebus.

easter_eggs.seed: Voss briefly touches the damaged lower-left plate of her armor before ordering the descent.
easter_eggs.payoff: The gesture is connected to Cinderline and appears whenever she is about to choose mission duty over rescue.

easter_eggs.seed: The gateway destination flickers for four frames with what looks like a human skyline.
easter_eggs.payoff: It is a future human settlement, not the abducted colony's current destination.
